description: Single source of truth for the site's cinematic clips, tier (b) of the motion language. scripts/generate-motion-clips.ts regenerates lib/motion-clips.ts (the registry the <Clip> component reads) and scripts/render-clips.ts reads the beats to build captions and the text alternative. Edit this file, then run npm run generate:motion-clips. The binding design input is docs/design/motion-language.md.

clips.title: One Kalman filter, a whole run
clips.headline: The filter keeps tracking, but grows less sure without readings
clips.teaches: Through noisy and missing readings the filter stays close to the object, and its band shows when a robot should trust it less.
clips.statusNote: Illustrative: a simulated run, not measured on hardware.

beats.caption: An object moves back and forth as time runs left to right, and the dashed line marks its true position.
A noisy sensor reports the object's position as dots, and about one time in five it reports nothing.
The filter's estimate, the solid line, stays close to the true position, and the shaded band shows how unsure it is.
While readings are missing the filter grows less sure and its band widens, which tells a robot to trust the estimate less.

method: A seeded toy simulation (seed 1): an object drifts along a line, and a position sensor reads it with random noise and misses about one step in five. The clip shows 240 steps of that run, steps 300 to 540, with time running left to right and position up and down.
Each step has two halves, which Kalman filters call predict and update: predicting where the object moved widens the band, and a reading, when one arrives, narrows it.
The band spans two standard deviations either side of the filter's estimate, about 95% of its belief. The filter's noise settings match the simulation: process noise 0.20, reading noise 1.00.

The note and its arrow mark steps 436 to 439, the longest run of missing readings in the simulation: four in a row, with that stretch of the band tinted in the note's colour. By the fourth missing step the band is three times as wide as at the last reading before the gap, and it narrows when the next reading arrives.
The clip is rendered offline from the same filter code as the scene above. It is silent; its captions and the transcript carry the words.
clips.textAlternative: Illustrative cinematic clip, 16 seconds: one Kalman filter over a whole run of 240 steps, with time running left to right and position up and down. Labels name each mark. An object moves back and forth; a dashed line marks its true position. A noisy sensor reports the object's position as scattered dots, and about one time in five it reports nothing. The filter's estimate, a solid line, stays close to the true position, and a shaded band around it shows how unsure the filter is: a wider band means less sure. A note reads: no readings, the filter grows less sure. Its arrow points at the band's widest stretch, tinted in the note's colour, where four readings in a row are missing and the band grows to three times its width; the next reading narrows it again. In filter terms, each predict step widens the band and each update with a reading narrows it. Simulated run, not measured on hardware.
